title: Coffee cooling towards room temperature
caption: T = T_a + (T₀ − T_a)e^{−kt} with T_a = 20 °C and T₀ = 90 °C. Falling to 60 °C in 10 min fixes k = ln(70/40)/10 = 0.056 min⁻¹. Then the coffee reaches 40 °C at t = ln(70/20)/k = 22.4 min. The curve flattens as it nears 20 °C: cooling is fastest when the difference from the room is largest.
alt: Graph of coffee temperature against time: an exponential decay from 90 °C towards 20 °C, passing 60 °C at 10 minutes and 40 °C at 22.4 minutes.
description: The horizontal axis is time in minutes; the vertical axis is the coffee temperature in °C.
The curve starts at 90 °C and decays towards the room temperature 20 °C with rate constant k = 0.056 min⁻¹.
At 10 min it is at 60 °C (this fixes k); it reaches 40 °C at 22.4 min.
